From f46f156ea7704a40577800c3df63b599121a87ec Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2017 17:46:52 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915/selftests: Only touch archdata.iommu when it exists

archdata.iommu only exists when CONFIG_IOMMU_API is enabled (and only
applies to intel-iommu in our case) so conditionally compile it out when
it doesn't exist.

Fixes: b5891fb520f7 ("drm/i915/selftests: Disable iommu for the mock device")
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Matthew Auld <matthew.auld@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20170918164652.14200-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk
Reviewed-by: Matthew Auld <matthew.auld@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/selftests/mock_gem_device.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/selftests/mock_gem_device.c
index 38ed006be5be..2388424a14da 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/selftests/mock_gem_device.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/selftests/mock_gem_device.c
@@ -146,8 +146,10 @@ struct drm_i915_private *mock_gem_device(void)
 	dev_set_name(&pdev->dev, "mock");
 	dma_coerce_mask_and_coherent(&pdev->dev, DMA_BIT_MASK(32));
 
+#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IOMMU_API)
 	/* hack to disable iommu for the fake device; force identity mapping */
 	pdev->dev.archdata.iommu = (void *)-1;
+#endif
 
 	dev_pm_domain_set(&pdev->dev, &pm_domain);
 	pm_runtime_enable(&pdev->dev);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `mock_gem_device.c`**
   - Added a conditional compilation directive `#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IOMMU_API)` to check if the `CONFIG_IOMMU_API` is enabled.
   - The line that sets `pdev->dev.archdata.iommu` to `(void *)-1` is now enclosed within this conditional directive, ensuring that this assignment only occurs if `CONFIG_IOMMU_API` is defined.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `mock_gem_device.c` is aimed at preventing the code from accessing `archdata.iommu` when the `CONFIG_IOMMU_API` is not enabled. This change is significant because it addresses a potential issue where the code could attempt to manipulate `archdata.iommu` in environments where it does not exist, which could lead to undefined behavior or compilation errors. The patch effectively ensures that the code is more robust and only interacts with `archdata.iommu` when it is safe to do so, thereby fixing the bug introduced in a previous commit (identified by the Fixes tag).

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
pdev->dev.archdata.iommu = (void *)-1;
```
Reason:
This line attempts to access and modify `pdev->dev.archdata.iommu` without checking if `CONFIG_IOMMU_API` is enabled. If this configuration is not enabled, `archdata.iommu` does not exist, leading to undefined behavior or compilation errors.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IOMMU_API)
pdev->dev.archdata.iommu = (void *)-1;
#endif
```
Reason:
The addition of the `#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IOMMU_API)` preprocessor directive conditionally compiles the code that accesses `pdev->dev.archdata.iommu`, ensuring that it is only included when `CONFIG_IOMMU_API` is enabled. This prevents the code from attempting to access a non-existent member, thus avoiding potential undefined behavior or compilation errors.
